commitResults.messageTitle: fix: Reject upper-case prefixes inside values
commitResults.messageBody:
Prefixes are recognised in any letter case after whitespace, so text
such as N/A, T/2 or S/E inside a value starts a new field. For
example, edit 1 a/Unit N/A renames the candidate to A without a
warning, and such text cannot be entered at all.

Neither reading is safe to guess when an upper-case prefix cuts into
a value typed with lower-case prefixes: #145 shows users mean
S/Offered as a field, while N/A is usually text.

Let's reject that case in add, edit and note with an error that
gives both fixes, and read \/ in any value as a plain slash so the
text can still be entered.

Commands typed entirely in upper case keep working, so the #145 fix
stays in place.

Fixes #253

commitResults.messageTitle: doc: Explain how to keep prefix-like text
commitResults.messageBody:
The guides say a prefix in any letter case always starts a new field,
and that edit 1 a/Unit N/A changes the candidate's name.

Let's describe the rejection of upper-case prefixes inside lower-case
values and the \/ escape in the User Guide, and record the design and
its manual tests in the Developer Guide.

commitResults.messageTitle: fix: Read \/ as / only in candidate text fields
commitResults.messageBody:
Every tokenizer reads \/ in a value as /. Role commands also go
through the tokenizer, so delete_role r/SRE\/Ops looks up SRE/Ops. A
role saved with \/ in its name by an earlier version can no longer be
reached, and a distinct role SRE/Ops would be deleted instead.

Let's read \/ as / only in the values that tokenizeWithValidation
checks: names, phones, emails, addresses, tags and notes. Role and
status values keep \/ as typed.

The tests that typed R/ after lower-case prefixes now put it first,
so upper-case R/ is still covered.

commitResults.messageTitle: doc: Limit the \/ escape to candidate text
commitResults.messageBody:
The guides say every \/ is saved as /, and the Developer Guide uses
edit 1 a/12 Kent Ridge Drive S/Offered as a command that sets the
status, although that mixed-case command is now rejected.

Let's state that \/ applies to names, phones, emails, addresses and
notes while role names keep it as typed, and use an all upper-case
example for the status case.

commitResults.messageTitle: fix: Suggest only the escape for repeated prefixes
commitResults.messageBody:
An upper-case prefix inside a lower-case value, such as the N/ in
a/Unit N/A, is rejected with two suggested fixes: N\/ keeps it as text,
and n/ starts a new field.

When the command already has that field, as in n/Bob a/Unit N/A, the
second suggestion only leads to a duplicate-prefix error, because n/
can be given once.

Let's suggest only the escape when the prefix is already a field and is
not one of the repeatable t/ and r/ prefixes, and say why in the error.

The tokenizer decides this because it builds the message. Only add and
edit accept repeated prefixes, and both repeat just t/ and r/, so one
set covers every caller.

commitResults.messageTitle: doc: Describe the escape-only prefix error
commitResults.messageBody:
The UG and DG say the ambiguous-prefix error always offers two fixes:
the escaped prefix keeps the text, and the lower-case prefix starts a
new field.

The error now offers only the escape when the command already has that
field and it cannot repeat, so the guides would mislead readers.

Let's describe that case in both guides, and update the manual test
for edit 1 s/Applied S/Offered to expect the shorter error.

commitResults.messageTitle: doc: Separate old and new prefix behaviour
commitResults.messageBody:
The Developer Guide's prefix-like text section mixes v1.5 behaviour
with the new rejection, so readers cannot tell whether the S/ example
is a problem or the intended result.

Let's state the v1.5 problem first, then list the current behaviour
with one example each, and explain why the rejection is needed
alongside the \/ escape.
